draft.title: The Terror
card: The Terror was a period in 1793 and 1794 when the government used fear and force to defend the revolution. France was at war with other European powers and faced revolt at home.
The Committee of Public Safety, a small group of leaders, held great power. It was backed by the Convention, the elected assembly.
The Law of Suspects of September 1793 allowed the arrest of people thought to be enemies of the revolution. Revolutionary tribunals tried them, and many were executed, some by the guillotine.
Its supporters said these measures were needed to save the republic from invasion and civil war. Tens of thousands died, and many more were held in prison.
draft.remember: The Terror used arrests and executions to defend a republic under threat from war and revolt.

a.q: Which statement best describes the purpose of the Terror, as its supporters saw it?
opts: To defend the republic from enemies at home and abroad
To restore the king to power after the war
To end the war by making peace with Austria
To return land and privileges to the nobles
a.why: Its supporters argued that war abroad and revolt at home meant harsh measures were needed to save the republic. Restoring the king would have ended the revolution, which the Committee wanted to defend.
a.clue: Ask who the Committee of Public Safety was trying to protect.

b.q: In 1793 Henri, a shopkeeper in Lyon, is arrested because neighbours say he opposes the revolution. Which measure allowed this?
opts: The Law of Suspects
The abolition of feudal dues
The Declaration of the Rights of Man
The Civil Constitution of the Clergy
b.why: The Law of Suspects allowed people thought to be enemies of the revolution to be arrested and tried. The Declaration of the Rights of Man proclaimed liberty, so it is a tempting but wrong choice.
b.clue: Which law was about arresting suspected enemies?

a.best: To defend the republic from enemies at home and abroad

problems.detail: The clue ('Which law was about arresting suspected enemies?') echoes the option name 'Law of Suspects', so a student can pick it by word-matching without knowing the idea.
The scenario says only 'In 1793', but the Law of Suspects was passed in September 1793. An arrest earlier that year could not have relied on it, so the scenario should be set after September 1793.
The distractors (restoring nobles' privileges, restoring the king, making peace with Austria) are plainly anti-revolutionary or off-topic, which makes the question too easy for Year 12.

a.q: Which statement best describes the purpose of the Terror, as its supporters saw it?
opts: To defend the republic from enemies at home and abroad
To punish the nobles for their past feudal privileges
To spread the revolution by conquering nearby states
To replace the elected Convention with a small committee
a.why: Its supporters argued that war abroad and revolt at home meant harsh measures were needed to save the republic. Some nobles were among the victims, but supporters justified the Terror as defence, not as punishment for the past. The Committee worked with the backing of the Convention rather than replacing it.
a.clue: Look at the dangers the card says France faced in 1793.

b.q: In November 1793 Henri, a shopkeeper in Paris, is arrested because neighbours say he opposes the revolution. Which measure allowed this?
opts: The Law of Suspects
The abolition of feudal dues
The Declaration of the Rights of Man
The Civil Constitution of the Clergy
b.why: The Law of Suspects, passed in September 1793, allowed people thought to be enemies of the revolution to be arrested and tried. The Declaration of the Rights of Man is a tempting choice because it is a famous revolutionary text, but it dates from 1789 and did not set up arrests of suspects.
b.clue: Which measure was passed during the Terror itself?
